lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital for 12 weeks (within 12-week limit)
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning a formal eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I'm starting the assessment process. To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to understand your situation first.

**Can you please tell me:**

1. **How many children** are you claiming for or want to inquire about?
2. **What is each child's age?**

This information will help me understand which eligibility path applies to you. Child Benefit rules differ depending on whether children are:
- **Under 16 years old** (automatic qualification if other conditions are met)
- **16-19 years old** (eligible if in approved education or training)
- **20 years old or over** (not eligible for Child Benefit)

Once you provide these details, I'll guide you through the specific eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and want to check if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, let me proceed with the next eligibility check. I need to ask you about Alex's employment status.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question for Alex:**

Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?

This is an important eligibility criterion - children cannot be working full-time (24+ hours per week) and be eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh no, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 8! He's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - Alex is in primary school and not working, so he meets that requirement. Let me continue with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question about Alex's benefits:**

Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

In other words, is Alex not claiming any of these benefits himself?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child - I'm the one who handles all that sort of thing for our family.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good! That makes sense - Alex is just a child and you're managing his needs. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question about Alex's apprenticeship status:**

Is Alex in an apprenticeship? Given that Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, I expect the answer is no, but let me confirm:

Is Alex NOT in an apprenticeship, or is he in any form of apprenticeship (which would be unusual at his age)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8! He's just in primary school, nowhere near old enough for an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Alex is far too young for an apprenticeship. Let me move forward with the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to check your residency status:**

This is an important eligibility requirement. There are several ways you can meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit. Let me ask you about your situation:

**Do any of the following apply to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - this is the most straightforward path
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** AND meet certain conditions (working, job-seeking, have sufficient resources, studying, or are a family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

Which of these best describes your situation? Or to keep it simple: **Do you normally live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm here in England with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK in England. That means you meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex:**

This checks whether you are legally responsible for the child. You can satisfy this in several ways:

1. **You live with the child** - you and Alex live together
2. **You contribute to the child's upkeep** - you pay at least as much as the Child Benefit amount towards their care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.)
3. **You're paying maintenance** - you make payments under a court order or agreement for the child's maintenance

**In your case, do any of these apply?** Most simply: **Do you live with Alex and are responsible for his upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me. I'm his parent and look after him - I provide everything he needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex and are responsible for him - that clearly meets the responsibility requirement. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question about other claimants:**

Child Benefit can only be claimed by one person per child. I need to check:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied for it?**

For example:
- The other parent
- A grandparent
- Another relative or guardian

If multiple people are eligible, only one can actually receive the benefit, so I need to understand your situation here.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm his parent and he lives with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So you're the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question about Alex's living situation:**

I need to check if Alex has any special circumstances regarding where he's living:

**Which of the following best describes Alex's current situation?**

1. **In hospital** - staying in hospital long-term
2. **In care** - in local authority care
3. **Fostered** - with foster carers
4. **Living normally at home** - with you in a normal home environment

Based on what you've told me so far, I expect it's the normal home environment, but let me confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in hospital for a while now - about three months. He's been having some medical treatment there.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that important information. Alex being in hospital does affect the eligibility assessment. Let me check the specific duration rules.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question about Alex's hospital stay:**

There are specific rules about how long a child can be in hospital while still being eligible for Child Benefit. I need to understand the details:

**About Alex's hospital stay:**

1. **Has Alex been in hospital continuously for about 3 months (12 weeks) now?** Or has he had multiple separate stays?

2. **Has Alex ever been in hospital before this current stay?** If so:
   - How long were those previous stays?
   - How long have the gaps been between hospital stays? (The rule is that if he returns to hospital within 28 days of leaving, previous stays count towards the 12-week total)

The important point is that Child Benefit can continue for up to 12 weeks in hospital, but it's calculated cumulatively - if there are multiple stays with gaps of less than 28 days, they all add together towards the 12-week limit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital continuously for about three months - just this one stay. He hasn't been in and out or had previous hospital stays.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex has been in hospital continuously for about 3 months (approximately 12 weeks) in this one stay, with no previous hospital admissions.

Let me check the next part of the eligibility criteria for children in hospital.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question about expenses while Alex is in hospital:**

There's an important exception to the 12-week hospital rule. Even if a child has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, Child Benefit can still continue if you are **regularly spending money on the child** while they're in hospital.

This can include things like:
- Visiting expenses (travel, accommodation)
- Clothing or toiletries
- Entertainment or comfort items
- Food or treats
- Other regular contributions to their care

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?** For example, visiting him, bringing him things he needs, or contributing to his comfort while there?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I still buy things for Alex while he's in hospital - I get him clothes, magazines, and his favorite snacks and treats when I visit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You are regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital - buying him clothes, magazines, snacks, and treats when you visit. That's an important factor. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final eligibility question:**

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he's in hospital?**

In other words, are you or another family member covering the costs, rather than the council paying for his hospital stay and care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - the hospital is just providing his medical care through the NHS, and I'm covering any extra things he needs myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's the final piece of information I need. Let me confirm your eligibility.

You have met all the requirements for Child Benefit:

1. ✅ **Qualifying child**: Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
2. ✅ **Not working full-time**: Alex is in primary school, not working
3. ✅ **Not receiving certain benefits**: Alex doesn't receive ESA or Universal Credit
4. ✅ **Not in disqualifying apprenticeship**: Alex is far too young
5. ✅ **UK residency**: You normally live in the UK (England)
6. ✅ **Responsible for child**: You live with Alex and provide for him
7. ✅ **No other claimant**: Only you are claiming
8. ✅ **Hospital situation handled correctly**: Although Alex has been in hospital for 3 months, you are regularly spending money on him (clothes, magazines, snacks, treats), which means Child Benefit can continue
9. ✅ **Council not paying**: The NHS is providing his medical care, and you're covering extra expenses yourself - the council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance

Now let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

**Result:** ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex

---

### **Summary of Your Eligibility:**

You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Here's what qualifies you:

✅ **Alex's age and status**: 8 years old, in full-time education, not working, not receiving other benefits
✅ **Your circumstances**: UK resident in England, parent with responsibility for Alex
✅ **Hospital exception**: Even though Alex is currently in hospital for approximately 3 months, you continue to be eligible because you are regularly spending money on him (clothes, magazines, snacks, treats) while he receives NHS treatment
✅ **No conflicting claims**: You're the only claimant for Alex
✅ **Council involvement**: The council is not paying for his accommodation - the NHS provides his medical care

---

### **Next Steps:**

1. **Make a claim**: If you haven't already, you can claim Child Benefit through the official government website at **www.gov.uk/child-benefit** or by phone
2. **Provide documentation**: You'll need to provide identification and proof of your responsibility for Alex
3. **Keep records**: Continue to keep documentation of your spending on Alex while he's in hospital, as this supports your continued eligibility
4. **Update when Alex leaves hospital**: Once Alex is discharged from hospital, let Child Benefit know if his circumstances change

---

### **Important Notes:**

- Child Benefit continues even while Alex is in hospital because of your regular spending on him
- If Alex's circumstances change significantly (e.g., if the local council starts paying for his care), you should report this to HMRC
- If you have any questions or need further support with your claim, contact HMRC's Child Benefit helpline

**Congratulations on your eligibility!** 🎉
